title: The permanent-address form labels its postcode and phone boxes differently from DR1, and drops DR1's hint about international dialling codes

finding.frontend: The frontend's permanent-address boxes are labelled Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postal or zip code, Country, Telephone number, Email address — from the commodities copy file at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:96-107, in that order. Three differ from DR1: "Postal or zip code" against DR1's "Postcode or Zip code", "Telephone number" against DR1's "Phone number", and the phone box carries no hint. The order differs too — the frontend puts the phone before the email, DR1 the other way round. No frontend capture shows this: the block is gated to Cat and Dog and the corpus captured cow, horse and fish.
finding.prototype: DR1's new-address fields are Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Email address, Phone number, and the phone box is hinted "For international numbers include the country code" — app/views/partials/permanent-address-new-address-fields.html:62-96. Six of the labels match the frontend exactly.
finding.difference: Relabel the postcode and phone boxes in copy.en.js:96-107 and its Welsh counterpart, add the international-dialling hint to the phone box, and swap the phone and email boxes so email comes first, in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/address/fields.js:126-163. One difference is deliberately not part of this change: the frontend has a Country select that DR1's permanent-address form has no equivalent of. Removing a country from an address that can be outside the UK is a designer's call, not a copy fix, so it is left where it is and named here so nobody has to rediscover it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a country field, or the label "Postal or zip code", in DR1's permanent-address new-address partial.
finding.verification: Opened dr1-permanent-address-animals, screenshot and rendered DOM — the address boxes sit inside the "Enter a new address" conditional reveal, so they are in the DOM and not in the picture — and read app/views/partials/permanent-address-new-address-fields.html whole: eight inputs, Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Email address, then Phone number hinted "For international numbers include the country code", and no country box anywhere. Checked the six-match count by hand against the frontend's list and it is six. On the frontend side read address/fields.js:117-163, which returns nine controls in the order given with the country as a select and no hint on any of them, and copy.en.js:96-107. Ran the falsifier: DR1's partial contains no country input and no "Postal or zip code" string, and DR1 hard-codes the country to "United Kingdom" when it formats one of these addresses for display (app/routes.js:2473). Established that the frontend block renders at all — traced in full on identification--permanent-address-placement. CORRECT.
finding.correction: Two notes, neither of which changes the claim. The frontend side is source-only in this corpus and the finding did not say so; the missing state is now named in finding.frontend. And the prototype citation :62-96 covers only the three boxes that differ, where the full eight-field list runs :7-96 — the range is left as it is because it points precisely at the differences the sentence is about, rather than nudged to cover prose it is not making a claim about.
